newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Synnex, Xander eye China PC market.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Synnex, Xander eye China PC market.

text.p: Taiwan's leading computer product supplier Synnex Technology International Corp on Thursday said it had acquired 80 percent of a Hong Kong-based firm to make inroads into the vast PC market in China.

"We have bought more than 80 percent of Laser Computer's shares, which would enable us to expand our business in Hong Kong and the mainland," Synnex senior manager J. J. Lin told Reuters by telephone.
He said Laser, which had 10 sales offices in China, distributing products of leading brands, including Intel, Seagate and Microsoft, was one of the major suppliers for China.
He said the acquisition would allow the company to make inroads into the highly potential computer market in China. He would not reveal the value of the deal.
China sold three million personal computers in 1996, three times more than the sales in Taiwan, Lin said.
Distributors in Taiwan have predicted sales will swell to 10 million sets in 2000.
Chinese statistics showed that China imported US$9.9 billion worth of computers and related equipment in that year, up 28.4 percent from 1995.

Another Taiwan supplier, Xander International Corp, said on Thursday that it was planning to set up offices in Hong Kong and the border Chinese city of Shenzhen on July 1. "We are highly interested in the vast mainland market, which has great potential," said Xander president Zachary Wu.

"After the Hong Kong and Shenzhen offices, we plan to open two other offices in Shanghai and Beijing before September and team up with local (Chinese) suppliers to form a large supply network," he told Reuters.
